q: 1. In PERT (Programme Evaluation & Review Technique) analysis the duration of the activities is taken as:
explain: PERT uses the expected mean time (calculated from the three time estimates) as the duration for scheduling calculations.

q: 2. Latest starts of an activity is always
options: greater than or equal to latest event time of preceding node
less than or equal to latest event tie of preceding node
equal to latest event time of preceding node
less than latest event time of preceding node
explain: Per the answer key, a.

q: 3. 'Wait' in PERT, belongs to the category of
explain: Waiting takes time, so it is an activity.

q: 4. An activity of the project is graphically represented by ……… on the network.
explain: Activities are arrows; events are circles.

q: 5. Which of the following statement is correct about the network diagram?
options: The events are represented graphically by circles or nodes at the beginning and the end of activity by arrows.
The tail end of the arrow represents the start of the activity
The head of the arrow represents the end of an activity
explain: All three are correct.

q: 6. Which operation must complete first?
options: Right of the line joining two circles
Left of the line joining two circle
explain: The operation on the left (the predecessor) completes first.

q: 7. Critical path method (CPM) requires:
explain: CPM uses a single deterministic time estimate for each activity, unlike PERT's three estimates.

q: 8. Number of pre-operation associated with an operation may be
explain: An operation can have one or more predecessors.

q: 9. The post-operations in CPM are marked
explain: Successors are marked to the right.

q: 10. In CPM method, the earliest finish is indicated by time on
options: top right, outside the circle, in triangle
top right, outside the circle, in rectangle
explain: Per the answer key, in a rectangle at the top right, outside the circle.

q: 11. CPM stand for:
explain: CPM stands for Critical Path Method.

q: 12. Latest finish time in CPM technique is indicated by a
explain: Per the answer key, a triangle.

q: 13. A bar chart is drawn for:
explain: A bar chart plots time against activities, with bar length representing each activity's duration.

q: 14. Dummy activities are used to
explain: Dummies maintain the required logic of the network.

q: 15. Which of the following are the guidelines for the construction of a network diagram?
options: Each activity is represented by one only arrow in the network
Dangling must be avoided in a network diagram
Dummy activity consumes no time or resource
explain: All three are network-construction guidelines.

q: 16. A CPM network is updated
options: whenever there is differences in the planned and actual performance
explain: Network updating is done whenever a deviation is found between planned and actual performance, requiring revision.

q: 17. In PERT, optimistic time represents the following time taken by an activity.
options: expected or average time taken when the activity is repeated several times
time taken if there is delay at every stage except due to natural calamities
minimum possible time taken under ideal conditions
most likely time taken under normal conditions
explain: Optimistic time represents the minimum possible duration an activity would take assuming everything goes ideally well.

q: 18. PERT stands for
options: Pertinent equation related to a task
explain: PERT stands for Programme Evaluation and Review Technique.

q: 19. Completion of an activity on CPM network diagram, is generally known
explain: Completion of an activity is marked by an event, represented as a node/connector point - all of above apply.

q: 20. Latest finish time CPM technique is indicated by a:
explain: In many CPM notations, latest finish time is indicated in a rectangular box associated with the node.

q: 21. Negative slack occurs:
options: When latest allowable time is greater than earliest expected time
When events stick to their schedule
explain: Negative slack typically results from a deficiency of resources causing schedule delays beyond the allowable time.

q: 22. Float may be defined as the difference between
options: latest start time and the earliest start time
latest finish time and the earliest finish time
time available and time required to complete the activity
explain: Float can be equivalently expressed via any of these differences (LST-EST, LFT-EFT, or available-required time) - all of the above are valid definitions.

q: 23. For completion of a project, the critical path of the network represents:
explain: The critical path represents the minimum time required to complete the entire project.

q: 24. Gantt chart is drawn for
explain: A Gantt chart plots activities against time, similar to a standard bar chart.

q: 25. An activity is
options: an element of work entailed in the project
the movement of heavy vehicles from one place to another
the beginning or the end of a specified job
the progress of work up to centrain limit
explain: An activity is an element of work in the project.

q: 26. An event is
options: the start and/or finish of an activity or the group of activities
explain: An event is the start and/or finish of activities.

q: 27. PERT technique of network analysis is mainly useful for:
explain: BUT AS PER BOOK C .PERT is a scheduling/planning technique, not related to tender inviting, opening, or awarding processes - hence none of the above.

q: 28. The pictorial representation of activities and events of a project is known as the
explain: It is called a network.

q: 29. The flow of time in a net work is generally
explain: Time flows left to right.

q: 30. Bar chart is also known as
explain: A bar chart is also called a Gantt chart.

q: 31. Bar chart is drawn for
explain: Per the answer key, time versus activity.

q: 32. When float or slack of an activity is positive, it represents
explain: Positive float indicates spare time is available for the activity, implying flexibility/availability of extra time (and by extension resources) without impacting overall completion.

q: 33. The pictorial representation of activities and events of a project is called
explain: The network diagram is the standard pictorial representation depicting a project's activities and events with their interrelationships.

q: 34. The object of technical planning, is
options: initiating the procurement action of resources
explain: Technical planning covers preparing specifications, estimates, and initiating resource procurement - all of the above.

q: 35. PERT technique of network analysis is mainly useful for
explain: Per the answer key, c. PERT suits R&D projects where activity times are uncertain.

q: 36. Select the correct statement
options: activity arrows in a CPM network are drawn to scale
the tail of an arrow represents the finish of an activity
arrow bead represents the start of an activity
explain: Arrows are not drawn to scale, the tail is the start, and the head is the finish, so a, b and c are all wrong.

q: 37. Inputs used during scope planning include all of the following except
explain: Scope planning inputs typically include the project charter, product description, and constraints, but detailed budget/cost analysis is not a direct input to scope planning.

q: 38. Which of the following is a weakness of bar chart?
explain: Per the answer key, all of the above.

q: 39. Which of the following is not a PERT event?
explain: 'Class is being attended' is an ongoing activity, not an event.

q: 40. In PERT analysis, the time estimates of activities and probability of their occurrence follow
explain: Per the answer key, a. Note: PERT normally assumes the beta distribution (c).

q: 41. A project has three independent critical paths A, B and C. To reduce the project length, we have to shorten
options: The activities of A, B and C
explain: When multiple independent critical paths exist, shortening the project duration requires reducing activities on all of them simultaneously (A, B, and C).

q: 42. Free float is mainly used to
options: identify the activities which can be delayed without affecting the total float of succeeding activity
identify the activities, which can be delayed without affecting the total float of succeeding activity
identify the activities which can be delayed without affecting the total of either the preceding of succeeding activities.
explain: Options a and b read almost identically in the book. Per the key, b.

q: 43. CPM requires
explain: CPM uses a single deterministic time estimate.

q: 44. PERT requires
explain: PERT uses three time estimates: optimistic, most likely and pessimistic.

q: 45. A milestone chart
options: shows the inter dependence of various jobs
shows the events in chronological, but in a logical sequence
explain: Per the answer key, c. Note: the book's wording drops 'not' (milestone charts do not show logical sequence).

q: 46. Time estimated time required to complete an activity is termed as
explain: The time needed to complete an activity is its duration.
